blurb: Fission and fusion designs — light-water workhorses, SMRs, molten salt, fast reactors, microreactors, and every major fusion approach — with capex, fuel-cycle, regulatory, and timeline context.
title: Nuclear Reactor Types: A Practical Reference
lede: Every reactor is a bet on a coolant, a fuel cycle, a regulator, and a decade. This guide catalogs {{N_ENTRIES}} designs across seven classes — from the light-water fleet that makes 9% of world electricity to the fusion approaches racing toward first power — with the capex, fuel, and timeline context that decides which bets pay.

facets.label: Fuel
facets.tip: Fuel cycle(s) the design runs on. LEU <5% enrichment · HALEU 5–20% (the supply-chain chokepoint for most advanced designs) · MOX/Pu = plutonium-bearing · D-T = deuterium-tritium fusion · Advanced fusion = D-D, D-He3, p-B11.

facets.label: Capex
facets.tip: Directional overnight capital cost per kW for recent or credibly projected builds. Western FOAK projects have landed 2–3× above these figures; Chinese, Korean, and Russian builds anchor the low end. Untagged where no meaningful estimate exists.

facets.label: Timeline
facets.tip: When meaningful new deployment is credible: Deployed = operating fleet today · ~2030 = first units this decade · 2030s / 2040s+ = realistic first commercial power · Legacy = no new builds expected.

facets.label: Regulatory
facets.tip: Licensing posture of the leading examples: Licensed & proven = operating under mature frameworks · Under construction = approved and building · In licensing = applications filed or construction permits in hand · Pre-licensing = design stage, no formal application · Retired = historic.
